title: A registry built by the Holder idiom

blocks.text: The Holder idiom (Bill Pugh) **keeps the instance in a private static nested class**. The JVM initializes that nested class **only when `getInstance()` first reads it**, and class initialization is thread-safe, so the instance is lazy without any lock. Using the outer class for anything else creates nothing.

items: `created()` (given) counts how many times the constructor has run.
`describe()` (given) is another static method; calling it must **not** create the instance.
The private constructor **refuses to run a second time** with an `IllegalStateException`, because reflection can call a private constructor.

cases.says: getInstance() returns the same registry every time, and the constructor has run once.
Calling another static method of ServiceRegistry does not create the instance; the first getInstance() does.
Calling the private constructor through reflection after getInstance() fails with IllegalStateException.
The instance sits in a static final field of a private static nested class, and the outer class keeps no static ServiceRegistry field.

concepts: The Holder idiom creates the instance only when getInstance first reads the nested holder class, because class initialization is lazy and thread-safe.
A Singleton has a private constructor, a static field holding its one instance and a static method that returns it.
Reflection can call a private constructor, so a class-based Singleton's constructor refuses to run a second time.
